finding: Reviewed nine remaining LLM/discovery/ontology benchmark primary sources and their indexed manuscript contexts. Scope restrictions, negative comparisons, observation layers and interface-study limitations are retained; no essential manuscript defect found in these scopes.
next_action: Continue exact-reader Q2 from semantic-review-18.json with the remaining 31 scholarly sources, then software/commercial/public-data records. Preserve narrow claim scopes and source versions; visual acceptance remains separate.

records.finding: The response test on PDF p5 concerns YES/NO model-answer proportions. Figure 2 and its discussion on p8 report variable-exchange agreement .510 for GPT-3.5 and .870 for GPT-4, with over 70 percent NO responses for GPT-4. The manuscript accurately separates answer variability and symmetry from independence tests in the banking observation law.

MAC combines affirmative/negative/judge debate with data-based discovery and metadata fusion. Appendix A uses causal sufficiency and no-cycle assumptions; these are not verified bank premises. The p8 single-agent comparison remains competitive mainly on the small five-node graphs at approximately half the cost, while harder graphs favor debate. The manuscript preserves that cost/complexity qualification and does not infer truth from agent agreement.

The Roadmap distinguishes question, causal/statistical target, assumptions and estimation. Medical examples explicitly discuss prevalent versus incident users and misaligned eligibility/assignment clocks; pp4-5 and 7 acknowledge that uncued responses are generic and may miss bias. The manuscript accurately treats banking transfer as a proposed application of design principles, not an autonomous banking validation.

The accessible OLMo/BLOOM corpus study associates relation mentions with prediction performance; controlled synthetic additions and reverse/negated relations probe reliance on those mentions. The context study uses model-generated positive/negative contexts with human assessment. The manuscript correctly retains corpus/model scope, separates relation recall from discovery, and notes that a contextual intervention may change the causal world rather than merely test invariance.

The system combines optional CPDAG/SEM analysis with editing and model suggestions. PDF p11 specifies six nonexpert students choosing three of nine edges at each successive interface stage, without changing prior edges; p12 reports 5/18, 7/18 and 1/18 errors. The manuscript accurately records the fixed order and changing edges, and expert concern about missing citations. These author results do not identify a randomized interface effect or validate graph premises.

NLPSCM processes observational batches, uses PAGs and answer histograms, and allocates noisy-model edge queries under a fixed budget. PDF pp10-11 compare the allocation with random selection. PDF p13 retains calibration, fully probabilistic graph inference, two-observed-variable confounder scope, interventions and theoretical bandit analysis as open directions. The manuscript correctly distinguishes sequential information acquisition from longitudinal treatment-policy identification and physical experiments.

The numerical LCM transformer assumes additive noise, stationarity, no latent confounders and lagged-only effects (p2). Its limitations explicitly state that it does not detect or correct assumption violations (p13). The manuscript preserves those restrictions and accurately distinguishes this numerical temporal model from a conversational language-model wrapper.

The ontology framework supplies modular loading, typing, taxonomy and relation tasks; reported performance varies by task/domain and retrieval/calibration behavior. Counts differ (177 versus 180 ontologies); requirements are developer-defined without agreement measures. The manuscript explicitly preserves these limits, uses the architecture as design evidence, and does not promote ontology relations into causal edges or bank-measurement truth. Repository-specific statements require their separate nonpaper review.

CausalDS separates hidden conceptual SCM variables, observation/proxy/calibration artifacts, public scenes and private scoring. The reported exam distinguishes content, nonidentification abstention, continuous estimation, interval scores/coverage and tool cost; p11 reports small interval-task samples and substantial undercoverage. The manuscript accurately borrows this separation as an evaluation design principle, labels model results author-reported, and makes no local reproduction or authentic-bank claim.
